patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: mesial-tilted impaction; buccal impaction; pulpitis. Treatment: extraction recommended; pulpitis management; crown defect restoration.
chief_complaint: The patient reports recurrent food impaction around tooth 48 for several years, causing intermittent discomfort.
present_illness: Over the past few years, the patient has experienced repeated food trapping at the site of tooth 48, prompting today’s evaluation.
past_medical_record: The patient denies any recent travel to high-risk areas, contact with COVID-19 cases, or systemic illnesses.
examination: Tooth 48 shows mesial impaction with carious lesions on contacting surfaces. Tooth 47 has a distal carious defect with cold sensitivity but no percussion pain, gingival inflammation, or mobility. Tooth 18 is buccally displaced with occlusal caries. Tooth 16 has a fractured enamel–dentin area with exposed dentin, negative cold and percussion tests, healthy gingiva, and no mobility.
radiographs_examination: CBCT reveals that the lesion on tooth 47 extends into the pulp chamber; no periapical pathology is noted for teeth 16, 18, or 48.
diagnosis:
* Tooth 48: Mesial impaction
* Tooth 18: Buccal impaction
* Tooth 47: Pulpitis
treatment_plan:
* Extract teeth 18 and 48
* Perform root canal therapy on tooth 47
* Restore tooth 16 with a crown or inlay
treatment_recommendations:
* Extraction of teeth 18 and 48 to resolve impaction issues
* Root canal therapy followed by post-core and crown on tooth 47
* Full-coverage restoration of tooth 16
management: For tooth 47, the patient was informed of the diagnosis, plan, costs, and prognosis and provided consent. Local anesthesia and caries removal were performed, revealing pulp exposure; a pulpotomy was placed with a devitalizing agent. A provisional restoration was placed and the patient scheduled for definitive root canal therapy in one week. For tooth 48, flap elevation, crown-root sectioning, atraumatic removal, socket irrigation, gelatin sponge placement, and single-suture closure were carried out. For tooth 18, surgical extraction with curettage and hemostasis using a gelatin sponge were performed.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms occur, return for root canal therapy. Follow standard post-extraction care and take prescribed antibiotics as needed. Suture removal in one week.

past_medical_record: Generally healthy with no systemic diseases or drug allergies.
examination: Teeth 35 and 45 have extensive distal occlusal caries with deep cavities, positive probing and cold tests, negative percussion, and no mobility. Teeth 36, 46, and 47 have occlusal and buccal pit caries, negative probing, cold, percussion tests, and no mobility. Tooth 14 has a history of root canal treatment with filling loss and extensive distal occlusal caries extending subgingivally, negative percussion. Tooth 15 has a resin filling with marginal caries, negative cold and percussion tests, and no mobility. Generalized heavy calculus and gingival redness with easy bleeding.
radiographs_examination: CBCT shows deep caries extending to the pulp chamber in teeth 35 and 45, with a low-density area at the apex of tooth 45. diagnosis: Teeth 35 and 45: Pulpitis; Teeth 36, 37, 46, 47: Occlusal and buccal pit caries; Tooth 14: Periapical periodontitis, tooth structure loss; Tooth 15: Deep mesial caries; Tooth 45: Periapical periodontitis.
treatment_plan: Root canal therapy and post-crown restoration for teeth 35 and 45; Resin fillings for teeth 36, 37, 46, and 47; Gingival recontouring, root canal retreatment, and post-core crown restoration for tooth 14; Initial caries removal and base filling for tooth 15, with root canal therapy if pulp exposure or post-filling pain occurs.

past_medical_record: Generally healthy, denies systemic diseases and drug allergies.
examination: Tooth 48 is unerupted, with no gingival abnormalities.
radiographs_examination: CBCT shows mesioangular horizontal impaction of tooth 48, with the crown near the cervical area of tooth 47's root; the crown is mostly covered by bone, the apex is not fully developed, and the root is near the inferior alveolar nerve canal.
diagnosis: Mesioangular horizontal low impaction of tooth 48.
treatment_plan: Extraction of tooth 48 is recommended.
management: For tooth 48, the patient and guardian were informed of the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% articaine was administered, a distal incision was made along tooth 47, a flap was raised to expose the bone surface, bone was removed with an ultrasonic bone knife, space was increased, the crown and root were separated with a dental handpiece, and the tooth was atraumatically extracted. The socket was irrigated with saline, a gelatin sponge and Palio were placed, and three sutures were applied for hemostasis. Sutures to be removed in one week.
medical_instructions: Strictly follow post-extraction care instructions, take oral antibiotics (self-supplied), and return for follow-up if discomfort occurs. Sutures to be removed in one week.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Dental caries; supernumerary tooth. Treatment: Resin restoration.
chief_complaint: Referred from orthodontics for tooth extraction.
present_illness: Referred from orthodontics, seeking extraction.
examination: Tooth 17 has buccal-occlusal caries, negative percussion, normal gingiva, and normal cold test. Tooth 24 is intact with normal gingiva and no other notable findings.
diagnosis: Tooth 17: Dental caries; Tooth 24: Supernumerary tooth.
treatment_plan: Tooth 17: Resin restoration.
management: For tooth 17, caries removal was performed using a high-speed handpiece and chemical gel, followed by cavity preparation. The area was cleaned, dried, etched, rinsed, and dried again. A bonding agent was applied, thinned, and cured. Resin was incrementally filled and cured, then shaped, adjusted, and polished. For tooth 24, local disinfection with povidone-iodine and infiltration anesthesia with prilocaine were administered. After anesthesia took effect, the gingiva was separated, the tooth was loosened, and extracted with forceps. Routine curettage of the extraction site and pressure hemostasis were performed.
medical_instructions: Return if discomfort occurs, bite on gauze for 40 minutes, avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours, eat after 2 hours, avoid hot foods and hard biting.

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: Gingivitis. Treatment: Supragingival scaling with ultrasonic and air polishing.
chief_complaint: The patient reports bleeding from the gingival margin of the anterior teeth while brushing for over a month, requesting dental cleaning.
present_illness: For the past month, the patient has experienced gingival bleeding during brushing and chewing, which stops with rinsing. The patient seeks treatment.
past_medical_record: No history of hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, hepatitis, or tuberculosis. No known allergies. No recent travel to high-risk areas or contact with COVID-19 cases.
examination: General oral hygiene is fair, with slight pigmentation on tooth surfaces. Significant calculus, especially on the lingual side of the lower anterior teeth and buccal sides of posterior teeth. Gingival margins are red, soft, and thickened with blunted papillae. Gingival sulcus depth: 1 mm, BI: 1, Dl: 1, no attachment loss.
treatment_plan: Supragingival scaling with ultrasonic and air polishing.
management: Oral hygiene instruction provided, including brushing techniques and flossing. The patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Plaque disclosing agent applied, followed by rinsing, air polishing, full-mouth supragingival scaling, polishing, and fluoride varnish application. Steam eye mask applied, and iodine glycerin used. Oral hygiene education reinforced.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Refrain from consuming pigmented beverages like coffee, tea, and cola, and avoid smoking. Maintain oral hygiene and use mouth rinse. Schedule regular check-ups and return if symptoms persist.

chief_complaint: The patient requests restoration for a defect in the upper right posterior tooth.
present_illness: One year ago, the upper right posterior tooth underwent root canal treatment and glass ionomer restoration at another clinic, and the patient now requests a crown restoration.
past_medical_record: Healthy.
examination: Tooth 14 shows discoloration on the occlusal surface with a white filling on the distal side, palatal cusp defect, negative for cold, probing, percussion, and mobility tests. No significant periodontal abnormalities. Tooth 45 has a distal carious lesion with extensive decay, irregular margins, dark brown color, soft texture, and mild probing pain reaching deep dentin. Percussion is negative, cold and heat tests are similar to control teeth, but significant pain occurs when stimuli enter the carious lesion, which subsides immediately after removal.
radiographs_examination: Tooth 14 shows adequate root filling with no periapical shadow. Tooth 45 shows deep caries.
diagnosis: Tooth 14: tooth structure defect. Tooth 45: deep caries.
management: For tooth 14, the patient was informed about the pros and cons of various restorative materials, associated costs, time, potential follow-up visits, and complications, and chose an all-ceramic crown restoration. Tooth preparation, post space preparation, and fiber post cementation were performed. Fine tuning, silicone impression, silicone bite registration, and temporary crown placement were completed. For tooth 45, caries removal under local anesthesia revealed pulp exposure. The cavity was cleaned, dried, etched, and lined with IROOTBP. Adhesive was applied, thinned, and cured. 3M-p60 resin was incrementally filled, cured, shaped, occlusion adjusted, and polished.
medical_instructions: Advise the patient to rest and avoid eating overly cold, hot, hard, or sticky foods. Return promptly if any loosening or discomfort occurs, and schedule an appointment before visiting.

The maxillary arch has mild crowding with a square arch form and lingual inclination of the upper incisors. Teeth 16, 17, 26, 11, and 21 have visible restorations. examination_cn: 口腔卫生状况一般，牙面可见少量色素附着。牙石++，尤以下颌前牙舌侧及双侧后牙颊侧为重。牙龈缘充血色红，质地松软，边缘厚钝，龈乳头圆钝，龈沟深度1mm,BI:1,Dl:1,无附着丧失。

medical_instructions_cn: 一周内禁进酸性食物，避冷热刺激。禁咖啡、茶、可乐等含色素饮品，禁止吸烟。保持口腔卫生，漱口水含漱。定期复查，不适随诊。

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: crown defect; deep caries.
chief_complaint: The patient requests restoration for a crown defect in the upper right posterior tooth.
present_illness: One year ago, the upper right posterior tooth underwent root canal therapy and glass ionomer restoration at another clinic. The patient now requests crown restoration.
past_medical_record: The patient is healthy.
examination: Tooth 14 shows discoloration on the occlusal surface, with a white filling on the distal side and a missing palatal cusp. Cold test negative, probing negative, percussion negative, no mobility. Periodontal status is normal. Tooth 45 has a distal carious lesion with irregular margins, black-brown color, soft texture, and mild pain on probing, reaching deep dentin. Percussion negative, cold and heat tests similar to control tooth, but sharp pain when stimulus enters the cavity, which subsides immediately after removal.
radiographs_examination: Tooth 14 shows adequate root canal filling with no periapical shadow. Tooth 45 has deep caries.
diagnosis: Tooth 14: crown defect. Tooth 45: deep caries.
management: For tooth 14, the patient was informed about various restorative materials, costs, time, potential follow-ups, and complications. The patient chose an all-ceramic crown. Tooth preparation, post space preparation, fiber post cementation, fine-tuning, silicone impression, bite registration, and temporary crown placement were performed. For tooth 45, under local anesthesia, caries removal exposed the pulp. The cavity was cleaned, dried, etched, rinsed, and dried again. IROOTBP was used as a liner, bonding agent applied, air-thinned, and light-cured. 3M-P60 resin was layered, light-cured, shaped, adjusted, and polished.
medical_instructions: Advise the patient to rest and avoid excessively cold, hot, hard, or sticky foods. If any loosening or discomfort occurs, schedule a follow-up appointment, preferably by phone.

management: For tooth 27, under rubber dam isolation, the temporary seal was removed, the pulp chamber was cleaned, and the root canal was prepared using the Protaper system. For tooth 15, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered. Caries removal was performed, enlarging the pulp exposure. The canal was explored, irrigated, dried, and temporarily sealed with Cervitron.

Tooth 14 had root canal treatment and filling years ago, now with filling loss and extensive distal occlusal caries extending subgingivally, negative to percussion. diagnosis: Pulpitis in teeth 35 and 45. Occlusal and buccal pit and fissure caries in teeth 36, 37, 46, and 47. Periapical periodontitis and tooth structure defect in tooth 14. Mesial proximal deep caries in tooth 15. Periapical periodontitis in tooth 45.

The root canal was filled with a non-arsenic devitalizing agent and clove oil, temporarily sealed, and scheduled for a one-week follow-up. For teeth 36 and 37, local infiltration anesthesia with 4% articaine was administered, rubber dam applied, caries removed, cavity preparation, etching, rinsing, drying, bonding agent application, light curing, and layered filling with 3M P60 composite were performed, followed by occlusal adjustment and polishing.

Follow-up in one week. For teeth 46 and 47, local infiltration anesthesia with 4% articaine was administered, caries removed, cavities prepared, rubber dam applied, acid etched, rinsed, dried, bonding agent applied and light-cured. 3M P60 resin was used for incremental filling, occlusion adjusted, and polished. For tooth 45, local infiltration anesthesia with 4% articaine was administered, caries completely removed, rubber dam applied, acid etched, rinsed, dried, bonding agent applied and light-cured. Resin was used to build up the distal wall, light-cured, occlusion adjusted, and polished. An arsenic-free devitalizing agent with eugenol was placed in the canal, temporarily sealed, with a follow-up in one week. Teeth 14 and 15 are scheduled for future treatment.

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: mesial-tilted impaction; buccal impaction; pulpitis. Treatment: extraction recommended; pulpitis management; crown defect restoration.
chief_complaint: The patient reports recurrent food impaction around the lower right posterior tooth for several years.
present_illness: Over the past few years, the patient has experienced repeated food trapping at the site of the lower right posterior tooth, prompting today’s evaluation.
past_medical_record: The patient denies any recent travel to high-risk areas, contact with COVID-19 cases, or systemic illnesses.
examination: Tooth 48 shows mesial impaction with carious lesions on contacting surfaces. Tooth 47 has a distal carious defect with cold sensitivity but no percussion pain, gingival inflammation, or mobility. Tooth 18 is buccally displaced with occlusal caries. Tooth 16 has a fractured enamel–dentin area with exposed dentin, negative cold and percussion tests, healthy gingiva, and no mobility.
radiographs_examination: CBCT reveals that the lesion on tooth 47 extends into the pulp chamber; no periapical pathology is noted for teeth 16, 18, or 48.
diagnosis:
* Tooth 48: Mesial impaction
* Tooth 18: Buccal impaction
* Tooth 47: Pulpitis
treatment_plan:
* Extract teeth 18 and 48
* Perform root canal therapy on tooth 47
* Restore tooth 16 with a crown or inlay
treatment_recommendations:
* Extraction of teeth 18 and 48 to resolve impaction issues
* Root canal therapy followed by post-core and crown on tooth 47
* Full-coverage restoration of tooth 16
management: For tooth 47, the patient was informed of the diagnosis, plan, costs, and prognosis and provided consent. Local anesthesia and caries removal were performed, revealing pulp exposure; a pulpotomy was placed with a devitalizing agent. A provisional restoration was placed and the patient scheduled for definitive root canal therapy in one week. For tooth 48, flap elevation, crown-root sectioning, atraumatic removal, socket irrigation, gelatin sponge placement, and single-suture closure were carried out. For tooth 18, surgical extraction with curettage and hemostasis using a gelatin sponge were performed.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms occur, return for root canal therapy. Follow standard post-extraction care and take prescribed antibiotics as needed. Suture removal in one week.

Tooth 15 has mesial-labial discoloration with marginal gaps, negative percussion, and cold tests, and no gingival abnormalities. examination: Tooth 23 has a deep wedge-shaped groove at the cervical area with black caries extending 1mm below the gingiva into the deep dentin. Positive response to probing and cold test with prolonged pain, negative percussion test. Generalized moderate gingival recession with bleeding on probing. Poor oral hygiene with a debris index (DI) of 1 and calculus index (Cl) of 1, indicating supragingival calculus covering less than one-third of the tooth surface, detectable attachment loss, and subgingival calculus with a bleeding index of 4, indicating profuse bleeding on probing. Gingiva is swollen and dark red with loss of stippling.
radiographs_examination: Moderate alveolar bone resorption throughout the mouth.
management: Tooth 23: The patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% articaine was administered. Caries removal was incomplete, leading to pulp exposure, followed by pulpectomy. The coronal third of the root canal was prepared with GG drills, and the canal length was determined to be 24mm using an apex locator. The root canal was prepared using a large taper technique up to F2. Ultrasonic irrigation with 1% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water was performed, and a trial fit of the master cone was taken. The canal was dried with paper points and obturated with gutta-percha and sealer. A post-operative radiograph confirmed proper obturation. Periodontal treatment included subgingival scaling and root planing under local anesthesia, irrigation with hydrogen peroxide and saline, and placement of Periochip. Oral hygiene instruction was provided.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Maintain oral hygiene with regular use of mouthwash. Schedule regular follow-ups and return if discomfort arises.

Attachment loss and subgingival calculus detected, with a bleeding index of 4, indicating profuse bleeding upon probing. Gingiva is swollen, dark red, and lacks stippling.

management: The patient was informed of the diagnosis, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis and consented to the treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered in the upper left quadrant, followed by subgingival scaling, root planing, and laser treatment. The area was irrigated with hydrogen peroxide and saline. Tooth 28 was extracted using forceps, and the extraction site was curetted and compressed for hemostasis. Oral hygiene instruction was provided, including brushing, flossing, and the use of interdental brushes.
medical_instructions: Strictly follow post-extraction care instructions. Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Maintain oral hygiene and use mouthwash. Schedule regular follow-ups and return if any issues arise.

Canals were prepared with large taper technique to size 35#06, irrigated with alternating sodium hypochlorite and saline, dried, and temporarily sealed with calcium hydroxide paste. For tooth 23, gingival recontouring and resin wall fabrication were performed under local anesthesia.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Chronic periapical periodontitis; pulpitis.
examination: Teeth 31, 32, 33, 41, 44 show no percussion or palpation sensitivity, and no exudate in the root canals. The mucosa in the apical region is not swollen or red. Teeth 11, 13, 21 have deep carious lesions reaching the pulp chamber, with no percussion sensitivity or mobility. Tooth 23 is a residual root with caries at the gingival level, no percussion sensitivity or mobility, and healthy gingiva.
diagnosis: Tooth 23: Chronic periapical periodontitis; Teeth 11, 13, 21: Pulpitis.
management: For teeth 31, 32, 33, 41, 44: Temporary seal removal, ultrasonic irrigation with 2.5% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water, master cone trial fitting, disinfection, drying with paper points, filling with IROOTSP and gutta-percha, post-operative radiograph confirmed proper filling. Glass ionomer restoration and occlusal adjustment recommended for full crown restoration. For teeth 11, 13, 21, 23: Rubber dam isolation, local anesthesia, pulp chamber access, pulp extirpation, electronic root canal length measurement (13: 25mm, 11: 22mm, 21: 23mm, 23: 20mm); root canal preparation with large taper technique to size 35#06; alternating irrigation with sodium hypochlorite and saline, drying, temporary filling with calcium hydroxide paste. For tooth 23: Local anesthesia, gingival contouring, resin-based provisional wall fabrication.
medical_instructions: Follow-up if discomfort occurs.

chief_complaint: The patient reports pain in the upper left anterior tooth when exposed to hot and cold stimuli for several days.
present_illness: The patient has experienced pain in the upper left anterior tooth upon exposure to hot and cold for several days, with increasing duration of pain, and seeks treatment.
past_medical_record: The patient denies having cardiovascular diseases such as hypertension or coronary heart disease; metabolic diseases such as diabetes or gout. The patient denies having infectious diseases like hepatitis, syphilis, or HIV. The patient denies having autoimmune diseases such as lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, or Hashimoto's thyroiditis. The patient denies having hormonal disorders like hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism. The patient denies having renal system diseases. The patient denies having psychiatric disorders. The patient denies any allergies to penicillin or metals. The patient denies any history of medication use. The patient denies a history of smoking.
examination: Tooth 13 shows a deep wedge-shaped groove at the cervical area with black caries extending 1mm subgingivally, reaching deep dentin; positive probing; positive cold test with prolonged pain; negative percussion. Generalized moderate gingival recession and bleeding on probing. Poor oral hygiene with a debris index (DI) of 1 and calculus index (Cl) of 1, indicating supragingival calculus covering less than 1/3 of the tooth surface, with detectable attachment loss and subgingival calculus. Bleeding index of 4, with gingival bleeding overflowing the sulcus, gingival redness, swelling, and loss of stippling.
radiographs_examination: Moderate alveolar bone resorption observed throughout the dentition.
management: For tooth 23, the patient was informed of the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% articaine was administered. Caries removal revealed pulp exposure, leading to pulpectomy. The coronal third of the canal was prepared with GG drills, and the canal length was determined to be 24mm using an apex locator. The canal was prepared with a large taper technique and machine files up to F2. The canal was irrigated with 1% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water using ultrasonic agitation. A trial fit of the master cone was taken, and the canal was dried with paper points before obturation with sealer and gutta-percha. A post-operative radiograph confirmed proper obturation. The patient was scheduled for restorative treatment in one week. Subgingival scaling and root planing were performed under local anesthesia in the lower half of the mouth, followed by irrigation with hydrogen peroxide and saline, and application of Perio medication. Oral hygiene instruction was provided, including brushing, flossing, and interdental brush use.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and hot or cold stimuli for one week. Maintain oral hygiene with regular mouth rinsing. Schedule regular follow-ups and return if symptoms persist.

diagnosis:

* Fillings for teeth 16, 26, 27
* Root canal therapy for teeth 12, 33

management: For tooth 12, local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered. A rubber dam was placed, caries removed, pulp chamber accessed, pulp roof removed, and canal orifices located. Pulp was extirpated, and the coronal third of the canal was prepared with GG drills. A #15 K-file was used to determine the canal length, confirmed by radiograph at 20mm. The canal was prepared using a large taper technique to F3, irrigated alternately with sodium hypochlorite and saline, ultrasonically agitated, dried, and temporarily sealed with calcium hydroxide paste. For teeth 16, 26, and 27, carious dentin was removed chemically to deep dentin without pulp exposure, shade matched, gingival retraction applied, proximal restoration system used, pulp protection, base placed, and resin filling applied. Occlusion was adjusted, and fillings polished.

management: Oral hygiene instruction, brushing technique guidance, and flossing instruction were provided. The patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis and gave consent. Oral hygiene education was reinforced.

chief_complaint: The patient reports missing teeth for several months.

examination: Teeth 46 and 47 are missing with well-healed gingiva and sufficient keratinized tissue. Oral hygiene is average. Normal mouth opening and temporomandibular joint function.

diagnosis: Partial edentulism at sites of teeth 46 and 47 (K08.100x002).
management: The patient was fully informed and consented to the treatment plan, signing the informed consent for oral implant restoration. Pre-operative antibiotics were administered. Standard disinfection and draping were followed by local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine. A horizontal incision was made along the alveolar ridge, full-thickness flap elevation, site preparation, and insertion of BEGO implants (4.5x11.5 mm) at sites 46 and 47 with cover screws. Tension-free suturing was performed, and post-operative radiographs confirmed implant positioning.
medical_instructions: Advise follow-up if discomfort occurs. Bite on gauze for 40 minutes, avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours, and start eating after 2 hours, avoiding hot foods.

examination: Teeth 15 and 24 have temporary materials in place, no percussion pain, healthy gingiva, and normal cold test response.
management: Temporary materials were removed from teeth 15 and 24, the tooth surfaces were polished, and porcelain veneers were tried in with paste. The patient was satisfied with the result. The veneers and tooth surfaces were treated with hydrofluoric acid etching for 90 seconds, rinsed, and dried. The veneers were ultrasonically cleaned with 95% alcohol for 90 seconds and dried. Silane coupling agent was applied and dried with hot air for 20 seconds. The teeth were etched, rinsed, dried, and isolated. Both the teeth and veneers were coated with bonding agent (Ivoclar Vivadent Variolink N system), and dual-cure resin cement was applied to the veneer surface. The veneers were positioned, cemented, and light-cured. Occlusion was adjusted, polished, and photographs were taken.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: chronic periodontitis. Treatment: systemic periodontal therapy.

Poor oral hygiene; Debris Index (DI): 1, Calculus Index (Cl): 1 indicating supragingival calculus covering less than 1/3 of the tooth surface, detectable attachment loss, subgingival calculus, and bleeding index: 4 indicating bleeding filling and overflowing the gingival sulcus. Gingiva is swollen and dark red with loss of stippling.

treatment_plan: Systemic periodontal therapy.

Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% articaine was administered in the upper left region, followed by subgingival scaling, root planing, and laser treatment. The area was irrigated with hydrogen peroxide and saline. Tooth 28 was extracted with forceps, and the socket was curetted and compressed for hemostasis. Oral hygiene instruction (OHI) was provided, including brushing, flossing, and interdental brush use.
medical_instructions: Strictly follow post-extraction care instructions. Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Maintain oral hygiene and use mouthwash. Schedule regular check-ups and return if discomfort occurs.

present_illness: The patient describes tooth mobility and shifting, with difficulty chewing for several months. There is bleeding during brushing but no significant pain.
past_medical_record: The patient is generally healthy with no systemic conditions or drug allergies.
examination: Teeth 11, 12, 13, 22, and 23 exhibit moderate to severe gingival recession, bleeding on probing, tooth mobility (grade II), and periodontal pockets with a depth of 5mm. Overall poor oral hygiene with a debris index (DI) of 1 and calculus index (Cl) of 1, indicating supragingival calculus covering less than one-third of the tooth surface. Bleeding index of 4, with profuse bleeding filling and overflowing the gingival sulcus. Gingiva is red and swollen, with a loss of stippling.
radiographs_examination: X-rays show moderate to severe alveolar bone resorption around teeth 11, 12, 13, 22, and 23.
treatment_plan: Systemic periodontal therapy for teeth 11, 12, 13, 22, and 23.
management: Teeth 11, 12, 13, 22, and 23 were treated with 3% hydrogen peroxide rinses, ultrasonic scaling, polishing, and irrigation with 3% hydrogen peroxide. Medication was applied, and periodontal splinting with fiber tape was performed in the anterior region.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Maintain oral hygiene with mouthwash rinses. Schedule regular check-ups and return if any discomfort arises.

present_illness_cn: 自述牙齿松动移位，咀嚼无力数月，刷牙有出血，无明显疼痛。
past_medical_record_cn: 患者体健。否认系统性病史。否认药物过敏。
examination_cn: 11,12,13,22,23号牙齿，牙龈中重度退缩，牙周探易出血，牙移位，松动度Ⅱ度，探及牙周袋，深度5mm。全口卫生情况差；软垢指数(DI):1.牙石指数(Cl):1=龈上牙石覆盖牙面不超过1/3，可探及附着丧失，可探及袋内牙石，出血指数：4=探诊后出血溢满并溢出龈沟，牙龈红肿，牙龈呈暗红色，附着龈点彩消失。
radiographs_examination_cn: 11,12,13,22,23号牙齿，X片显示牙齿中重度牙槽骨吸收。
management_cn: 11,12,13,22,23号牙齿，3%双氧水含漱，超声洁治、抛光，3%双氧水冲洗，上药。前牙区行纤维带牙周固定。
medical_instructions_cn: 一周内禁进酸性食物，避冷热刺激。保持口腔卫生，漱口水含漱。定期复查，不适随诊。
anomalies_cn: 牙周炎,牙齿松动,牙龈炎

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: periodontitis.
chief_complaint: The patient reports discomfort due to mobility and poor color of the upper front teeth.
examination: Teeth 11, 21, and 22 have bioalloy restorations with poor marginal fit, gingival recession, and exposed roots. Probing reveals soft, dark material. Tooth 12 shows brown soft material on both mesial and distal surfaces, with gingival recession and root exposure. Teeth 13 and 23 have deep periodontal pockets on the mesial surfaces, measuring 4mm, with subgingival calculus.
radiographs_examination: X-rays show alveolar bone resorption around teeth 11, 12, 13, 22, and 23, with bone loss reaching the middle third of the roots of teeth 11, 12, and 22.
treatment_recommendations: Periodontal treatment for teeth 11, 12, 13, 22, and 23. Consider removing the fixed bridge on teeth 11, 21, and 22. Retain teeth 11, 12, and 22 if periodontal condition improves; extract if mobility worsens. Plan for fixed bridge restoration on teeth 11, 12, 13, 21, 22, and 23.
management: Under local anesthesia, supragingival scaling, subgingival curettage, and root planing were performed on teeth 11, 12, 13, 22, and 23. Alginate impressions were taken for diagnostic wax-up. Medication was applied.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard objects. Return for follow-up in one week.

chief_complaint: The patient reports bleeding from the gingival margin of the front teeth during brushing for over a month and requests dental cleaning.
present_illness: For the past month, the patient has experienced gingival bleeding during brushing and chewing, which stops with rinsing. The patient seeks treatment.
past_medical_record: No history of hypertension, heart disease, or diabetes. No history of hepatitis, tuberculosis, or contact with infectious diseases. No allergies reported. No recent travel to high-risk areas or contact with COVID-19 cases.
examination: Oral hygiene is average, with slight pigmentation on tooth surfaces. Calculus is present, especially on the lingual side of lower anterior teeth and buccal sides of posterior teeth. Gingival margins are congested, red, soft, with thickened and blunt edges. Gingival papillae are rounded, gingival sulcus depth is 1 mm, with bleeding index of 1, and no attachment loss.
treatment_plan: Supragingival scaling with ultrasonic and air polishing.
management: Oral hygiene education provided, including brushing techniques and flossing. The patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Plaque disclosing solution was applied, followed by rinsing, air polishing, full-mouth supragingival scaling, enamel polishing, and application of fluoride varnish. A steam eye mask was used, and iodine glycerin applied. Oral hygiene instructions were reinforced.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Avoid colored drinks like coffee, tea, and cola, and refrain from smoking. Maintain oral hygiene and use mouthwash. Schedule regular check-ups and return if symptoms persist.

chief_complaint: Referred from orthodontics for further dental treatment.
examination: Teeth 17 and 37 show occlusal fissure staining resembling ink infiltration. Negative to probing, percussion, mobility, and gingival inflammation. Cold test is normal.
treatment_plan: Restorative treatment for teeth 17 and 37.
management: For teeth 17 and 37, 1.2 ml of 4% Articaine was administered via local infiltration anesthesia. Rubber dam isolation was applied. High-speed handpiece was used to remove unsupported enamel and open the cavities. Most carious tissue was removed, the cavities were irrigated, and slow-speed excavation was performed to remove remaining caries. Cavities were disinfected with alcohol-soaked cotton pellets, etched with acid, rinsed, and dried. Bonding agent was applied twice and light-cured for 20 seconds. Flowable resin was used as a base, followed by aesthetic Italian resin layered restoration. Light curing was performed, rubber dam was removed, and occlusion was adjusted and polished.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs.

management: For tooth 24, under rubber dam isolation, the temporary sealing material was removed, the pulp chamber was cleaned, and the root canals were prepared using the Protaper system with SX files for the upper two-thirds and 10# K-files with an apex locator to determine canal lengths (buccal root 21mm, palatal root 19mm). The canals were irrigated with 2.5% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water, then sealed with calcium hydroxide and temporarily closed. For tooth 36, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to the treatment. Temporary crowns and sealing materials were removed, abutment teeth and restorations were cleaned, and the fit of the new restorations was checked. The fit was satisfactory, and the patient was pleased. Dual-cure resin cement was used for final cementation, occlusion was adjusted, and the restorations were polished.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard objects, maintain oral hygiene, and return for follow-up as needed.

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: Gingivitis. Treatment: Supragingival ultrasonic scaling and air polishing.
chief_complaint: The patient reports bleeding from the gingival margins of the front teeth during brushing for over a month and requests cleaning.
present_illness: For the past month, the patient has experienced gingival bleeding while brushing and chewing, which stops with rinsing. The patient now seeks treatment.
past_medical_record: No history of hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, hepatitis, tuberculosis, or allergies. No recent travel to high-risk areas or contact with COVID-19 cases.
examination: Oral hygiene is average with slight pigmentation on teeth surfaces. Heavy calculus is present, especially on the lingual side of the lower anterior teeth and buccal sides of the posterior teeth. Gingival margins are congested, red, soft, with blunt edges and rounded papillae. Gingival sulcus depth is 1 mm, BI:1, DI:1, with no attachment loss.
treatment_plan: Supragingival ultrasonic scaling and air polishing.
management: Oral hygiene education was provided, including brushing techniques and flossing. The patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to the treatment. Plaque disclosing agent was applied, followed by rinsing, air polishing, full-mouth supragingival scaling, and polishing. Enamel sealing for caries prevention was performed, and the patient was given an eye mask and iodine glycerin. Oral hygiene education was reinforced.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for a week. Refrain from consuming pigmented beverages like coffee, tea, and cola, and avoid smoking. Maintain oral hygiene and use mouthwash. Schedule regular check-ups and return if any discomfort occurs.

present_illness: The patient reports no discomfort following the treatment of the upper right anterior tooth two weeks ago and is here for follow-up.
examination: Tooth 12 shows no percussion pain or gingival inflammation. Temporary sealing is present. Tooth 34 is rotated and buccally positioned with a large carious lesion on the proximal surface extending to dentin. Tooth 33 has a deep carious lesion on the proximal surface extending to deep dentin with cold-induced pain.
diagnosis: Pulpitis of teeth 12 and 33 (K04.005); deep caries of tooth 34 (K02.800x008).
management: For tooth 12, temporary sealing was removed, post space preparation was done, and a resin fiber post was bonded. The abutment was prepared and refined. Silicone impressions and bite registrations were taken for temporary crown fabrication. For tooth 33, local infiltration anesthesia with 4% articaine was administered. Pulp chamber access was gained, pulp extirpated, rubber dam applied, and canal orifices located. The coronal third was prepared with GG drills, and the canal length was determined to be 20mm using an apex locator. Canal preparation was completed with rotary files to F2, followed by alternating irrigation with sodium hypochlorite and saline, drying, and temporary sealing with calcium hydroxide paste. For tooth 34, local disinfection with povidone-iodine and infiltration anesthesia with prilocaine were administered. After anesthesia onset, the gingiva was separated, the tooth luxated, and extracted with forceps. The socket was curetted and hemostasis achieved by pressure.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if any discomfort occurs. Bite on cotton roll for 40 minutes, avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours, and refrain from eating for 2 hours. Consume food that is not too hot.

management: For tooth 12, temporary seal removal, post space preparation, resin fiber post bonding, and abutment preparation were performed. management: For tooth 35, informed consent was obtained, and the patient signed the informed consent form for oral implant restoration. The site was prepared to the predetermined depth, and a Nobel implant (4.3x10 mm) was placed with a cover screw. Bone graft and membrane were applied, and tension-free sutures were placed. Postoperative radiographs confirmed the position.
medical_instructions: Strictly follow post-implantation care instructions, take oral antibiotics, and return for follow-up if any discomfort occurs. Sutures to be removed in two weeks.

chief_complaint: Continued restoration of the upper left anterior tooth, referred by Dr. Wei.

diagnosis: Tooth 22: Tooth structure defect, distal proximal caries.
treatment_plan: Crown restoration for tooth 22.
management: The patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to the treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered. Caries removal and cavity preparation were performed, reaching near the pulp chamber. After cleaning the cavity, a light-cured base was applied, followed by etching, rinsing, drying, and bonding agent application. The cavity was filled with 3M Z350 resin in layers, occlusion adjusted, and polished. Tooth preparation was completed, gingival retraction and refinement were done, silicone impressions and occlusal records were taken, and a temporary crown was fabricated and cemented with DMG temporary cement. Occlusion was adjusted, polished, and shade 2M2 was selected for an Emax all-ceramic crown.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms occur, root canal treatment may be necessary. Return for follow-up if any discomfort arises.

radiographs_examination: Generalized moderate to severe alveolar bone loss.
treatment_plan: Systemic periodontal therapy.

medical_instructions: Follow post-extraction instructions, take oral antibiotics as needed. Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Maintain oral hygiene with mouthwash. Regular check-ups and return if discomfort occurs.

examination: Tooth 48 shows mesial impaction with carious lesions on contacting surfaces. Tooth 47 has a distal carious defect with cold sensitivity but no percussion pain, gingival inflammation, or mobility. Tooth 18 is buccally displaced with occlusal caries. Tooth 16 has a fractured enamel–dentin area with exposed dentin, negative cold and percussion tests, healthy gingiva, and no mobility.
radiographs_examination: CBCT reveals that the lesion on tooth 47 extends into the pulp chamber; no periapical pathology is noted for teeth 16, 18, or 48.
diagnosis:
* Tooth 48: Mesial impaction

* Tooth 47: Pulpitis
treatment_plan:
* Extract teeth 18 and 48
* Perform root canal therapy on tooth 47
* Restore tooth 16 with a crown or inlay
treatment_recommendations:
* Extraction of teeth 18 and 48 to resolve impaction issues
* Root canal therapy followed by post-core and crown on tooth 47
* Full-coverage restoration of tooth 16
management: For tooth 47, the patient was informed of the diagnosis, plan, costs, and prognosis and provided consent. Local anesthesia and caries removal were performed, revealing pulp exposure; a pulpotomy was placed with a devitalizing agent. A provisional restoration was placed and the patient scheduled for definitive root canal therapy in one week. For tooth 48, flap elevation, crown-root sectioning, atraumatic removal, socket irrigation, gelatin sponge placement, and single-suture closure were carried out. For tooth 18, surgical extraction with curettage and hemostasis using a gelatin sponge were performed.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms occur, return for root canal therapy. Follow standard post-extraction care and take prescribed antibiotics as needed. Suture removal in one week.

examination: Tooth 22 shows a large incisal defect with a pulp exposure, percussion positive, and cold test painful. Tooth 13 is temporarily sealed with minimal food debris, percussion negative, no fresh exudate in the canal. Generalized moderate to severe gingival recession with bleeding on probing, tooth mobility grades I/II/III, periodontal pockets up to 5mm. Poor oral hygiene with plaque index (Dl): 1, calculus index (Cl): 1, and bleeding index: 4. Teeth 24 and 25 have root stumps at gingival level with soft, dark material, gingival redness, and easy bleeding.
radiographs_examination: Teeth 24 and 25 show low-density apical images.
diagnosis: Chronic periodontitis; apical periodontitis and retained roots on teeth 24, 25; pulpitis on tooth 22.
treatment_plan: Systematic periodontal therapy.
management: For tooth 22, the patient was informed of the diagnosis, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis and consented to treatment. Local anesthesia was administered, caries were partially removed, pulp exposure was managed, canal length was established at 19mm, and the canal was cleaned, irrigated, dried, and medicated, followed by temporary sealing with Cervitron. For tooth 13, under rubber dam isolation, the cotton pellet was removed, the canal was ultrasonically irrigated with 2.5% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water, and the master cone was prepared. The canal was dried with paper points and filled with SP and gutta-percha using vertical compaction, followed by temporary sealing with glass ionomer. Post-operative radiographs confirmed adequate filling. For teeth 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 21, 22, and 23, local anesthesia was administered, and supragingival scaling, root planing, and polishing were performed. For teeth 24 and 25, local anesthesia was administered, gingival separation, luxation, and extraction were performed, followed by curettage, saline irrigation, and placement of a gelatin sponge for hemostasis.

examination: Tooth 46 presents with deep occlusal caries, positive to probing, slight percussion sensitivity, positive cold test, no mobility, and normal gingiva. Tooth 36 shows occlusal caries reaching the middle dentin layer, negative to probing, percussion, and mobility, with a variable cold test and normal gingiva.
radiographs_examination: Tooth 46 shows a low-density shadow extending to the pulp, with no periapical abnormalities.
diagnosis: Tooth 46: Chronic pulpitis. Tooth 36: Moderate caries.

medical_instructions: Return for follow-up in 10 days. Avoid chewing on the affected side. Seek care if discomfort occurs.
remarks: Next visit for root canal preparation.

examination: Tooth 48 shows mesial impaction with carious lesions on contacting surfaces. Tooth 16 has a fractured enamel–dentin area with exposed dentin, negative cold and percussion tests, healthy gingiva, and no mobility.
radiographs_examination: CBCT reveals that the lesion on tooth 47 extends into the pulp chamber; no periapical pathology is noted for teeth 16, 18, or 48.
diagnosis: Tooth 48: Mesial-tilted impaction; Tooth 18: Buccal impaction; Tooth 47: Pulpitis.
treatment_plan: Extract teeth 18 and 48; Perform root canal therapy on tooth 47; Restore tooth 16 with a crown or inlay.
treatment_recommendations: Extraction of teeth 18 and 48 to resolve impaction issues; Root canal therapy followed by post-core and crown on tooth 47; Full-coverage restoration of tooth 16.
management: For tooth 47, the patient was informed of the diagnosis, plan, costs, and prognosis and provided consent. Local anesthesia and caries removal were performed, revealing pulp exposure; a pulpotomy was placed with a devitalizing agent. A provisional restoration was placed and the patient scheduled for definitive root canal therapy in one week. For tooth 48, flap elevation, crown-root sectioning, atraumatic removal, socket irrigation, gelatin sponge placement, and single-suture closure were carried out. For tooth 18, surgical extraction with curettage and hemostasis using a gelatin sponge were performed.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms occur, return for root canal therapy. Follow standard post-extraction care and take prescribed antibiotics as needed. Suture removal in one week.

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: Pulpitis; Deep caries.
chief_complaint: The patient reports blackened carious lesions on the upper anterior teeth for several days.
present_illness: The patient noticed blackened carious lesions on the upper anterior teeth for several days, affecting aesthetics, prompting today's visit.
past_medical_record: Healthy.
examination: Teeth 12 and 22 show extensive structural loss with brown carious lesions and pulp exposure, gingival overgrowth into cavities. Teeth 11 and 21 have interproximal discoloration reaching deep dentin. Teeth 14, 15, and 24 show similar interproximal changes. Teeth 16, 26, 37, and 47 have occlusal caries reaching dentin. Anterior crossbite noted.
radiographs_examination: Teeth 12 and 22 show caries extending to the pulp. Teeth 11, 14, 15, and 21 show caries approaching the pulp.
diagnosis: Teeth 12 and 22: Pulpitis. Teeth 11, 14, 15, 21, and 24: Deep caries.
management: For teeth 12 and 22, local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered. Rubber dam isolation, caries removal, pulp exposure, and pulp chamber access were performed. Canal orifices were located, and pulp extirpation was done. Canal preparation was completed using GG drills and rotary files to F3, with sodium hypochlorite and saline irrigation. Calcium hydroxide paste was used for temporary sealing. For teeth 11 and 21, local infiltration anesthesia was administered, caries removal exposed the pulp, and a biocompatible pulp capping agent was applied, followed by layered composite restoration. The patient was informed of the need for root canal treatment if postoperative pain occurs.
medical_instructions: Return if any discomfort occurs.

Took trial point radiographs for teeth 11, 21, 23, disinfected master points. Isolated, dried with paper points, filled with sp+gutta-percha, and took post-op radiographs. Temporarily sealed and placed temporary crowns, adjusted occlusion, and polished.

management: For tooth 23, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine was administered, caries was removed, and the pulp was extirpated. The coronal third of the canal was prepared with GG drills, the canal length was determined with an 08#C file and apex locator at 25mm, and the canal was prepared with a large taper technique to F3. The canal was ultrasonically irrigated with 1% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water, alternately flushed with sodium hypochlorite and saline, dried, and temporarily sealed with calcium hydroxide paste.
medical_instructions: Return if discomfort occurs. Avoid biting hard objects and return for a follow-up in one week.

examination: Teeth 45 and 46 are in the same condition as the previous visit.
management: For tooth 45, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to the treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered. Caries were completely removed, a matrix band was placed, etching was done, and the area was isolated after rinsing and drying. A bonding agent was applied and light-cured. 3M P60 resin was used for layered filling, light-cured, occlusion adjusted, and polished. Shofu resin was used for layered buildup of the mesial wall, light-cured, occlusion adjusted, and polished. Pulpotomy was performed, arsenic-free devitalizing agent and eugenol cotton pellet were placed, and the tooth was temporarily sealed. Follow-up in one week.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms occur, return for root canal therapy. Follow up if any discomfort arises.

chief_complaint: The patient reports bilateral posterior tooth pain for two weeks.

past_medical_record: Denies any systemic medical history.
examination: Teeth 38 and 48 have extensive occlusal caries reaching the pulp chamber, with distal gingival coverage. No response to cold or heat tests. Teeth 37 and 47 have proximal caries reaching deep dentin, with pain on cold and heat tests, and positive probing.
diagnosis: Teeth 37 and 47: Pulpitis; Tooth 48: Apical periodontitis; Tooth 38: Mesial impaction.
treatment_plan: Root canal therapy for teeth 37 and 47; extraction of teeth 38 and 48.
management: For tooth 47, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered, caries were partially removed, exposing the pulp with significant bleeding. The pulp exposure was enlarged, and a non-arsenic devitalizing agent was applied, followed by temporary sealing with Cervitron. For tooth 48, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and risks, and requested extraction. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered, gingival separation, space expansion, luxation, extraction with forceps, curettage, saline irrigation, gelatin sponge placement, and suture with pressure hemostasis were performed.
medical_instructions: Follow-up if discomfort occurs. Bite on gauze for 40 minutes, avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours, and eat after 2 hours, avoiding hot foods.

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: Gingivitis. Treatment: Supragingival scaling with ultrasonic and air polishing.
chief_complaint: The patient reports bleeding from the gingival margin of the front teeth while brushing for over a month, requesting dental cleaning.
present_illness: For the past month, the patient has experienced gingival bleeding during brushing and chewing, which stops with rinsing, and is now seeking treatment.
past_medical_record: No history of hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, hepatitis, or tuberculosis. No known allergies. No recent travel to high-risk areas or contact with COVID-19 cases.
examination: General oral hygiene is average, with slight pigmentation on tooth surfaces. Heavy calculus, especially on the lingual side of the lower anterior teeth and buccal side of the posterior teeth. Gingival margins are red, soft, and thickened, with blunt papillae. Gingival sulcus depth is 1 mm, BI:1, DI:1, with no attachment loss.
treatment_plan: Supragingival scaling with ultrasonic and air polishing.
management: Oral hygiene education was provided, including brushing techniques and flossing. The patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Plaque disclosing agent was applied, followed by rinsing, air polishing, full-mouth supragingival scaling, and polishing. Enamel sealing for caries prevention was done, along with steam eye mask application and iodine glycerin application. Oral hygiene education was reinforced.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Avoid pigmented drinks like coffee, tea, and cola, and refrain from smoking. Maintain oral hygiene and use mouthwash. Schedule regular check-ups and follow-up if discomfort occurs.

Dual-cure resin cement was used for final cementation, occlusion was adjusted, and polishing was done.

management: For tooth 47, the original filling was removed, the cavity was prepared, cleaned, and dried. Acid etching was performed, followed by rinsing and drying. examination: Tooth 22 has a porcelain crown with grade three mobility and a fracture extending subgingivally, no percussion sensitivity. Tooth 12 shows mesial incisal angle loss with lingual filling present, no percussion sensitivity, gingival swelling, and easy bleeding on probing. Teeth 11 and 21 show ink-like interproximal changes with probe retention reaching deep dentin. Teeth 17 and 18 show ink-colored carious lesions in fissures, probe retention reaching the pulp chamber, with extensive tooth structure loss in tooth 18.
radiographs_examination: Tooth 22 shows crown fracture. Teeth 11 and 21 have carious lesions reaching deep dentin. Tooth 12 has completed root canal treatment. Teeth 17 and 18 show carious lesions involving the pulp.
diagnosis: Tooth 22: Tooth fracture (K02.401). Teeth 11 and 21: Deep caries in permanent teeth (K02.800x008). Teeth 17 and 18: Pulpitis (K04.005). Tooth 12: Secondary caries (K02.800x001).
treatment_plan: Tooth 22: Extraction and implant placement. Teeth 11 and 21: Filling. Tooth 12: Crown restoration. Tooth 17: Inlay restoration post-root canal treatment. Tooth 18: Extraction.
management: For teeth 11 and 21, chemical gel was used to remove caries reaching deep dentin without pulp exposure, shade matching was done, gingival retraction applied, proximal restoration system used, pulp protection provided, base placed, layered resin filling completed, occlusal morphology restored, occlusal adjustment performed, and polished. For tooth 12, resin filling was done, abutment prepared, and refined. Silicone impression and bite registration were taken, and a temporary crown was fabricated. For tooth 17, under 4% articaine 1.7ml local infiltration anesthesia, pulp chamber was accessed, irrigated, hemostasis achieved, dried, and VOCO-Depulpin pulp devitalizer temporarily sealed. For tooth 18, local povidone-iodine disinfection and infiltration anesthesia with Bilocaine were administered. After anesthesia onset, gingival separation was performed, tooth loosened and extracted with forceps. Routine curettage of extraction site and pressure hemostasis were performed. For tooth 22, impressions were taken for custom-made invisible dentures.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Supernumerary tooth. Treatment: Extraction recommended.
chief_complaint: Referred for orthodontic extraction of a maxillary supernumerary tooth.
present_illness: Consistent with previous history. Radiographic examination revealed a supernumerary tooth in the maxilla requiring extraction.
past_medical_record: Generally healthy, with no history of systemic diseases or drug allergies.
examination: Tooth 21 shows no abnormalities on the palatal gingiva.
radiographs_examination: CBCT reveals an inverted supernumerary tooth at the apical third of tooth 21, with the crown oriented towards the root of tooth 11, measuring approximately 14mm in length and 5mm in width.
treatment_plan: Extraction of the supernumerary tooth near teeth 11 and 21.
management: Informed consent obtained from the patient and guardian regarding the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered. A vertical incision of approximately 10mm was made along the midline of tooth 11, and a horizontal incision of approximately 10mm was made 4mm lingual to teeth 21 and 22. A flap was raised to expose the palatal bone, and a small hole of about 6mm in diameter was drilled to expose the supernumerary tooth. The tooth was extracted atraumatically, and the socket was inspected for abnormalities. The area was irrigated with saline, sutured with four stitches, and hemostasis was achieved.
medical_instructions: Strict adherence to post-extraction care instructions. Oral antibiotics (self-provided) as needed. Follow-up for suture removal in one week.

present_illness: The patient has noticed darkening of the front tooth over several months without significant spontaneous symptoms and seeks treatment.
past_medical_record: No significant medical history.
examination: Tooth 13 exhibits extensive carious lesions on the mesial and labial surfaces with pulp exposure, eliciting significant pain on probing (++), negative cold test, and no percussion sensitivity. Tooth 12 has crown damage extending to the cervical third with extensive dark caries and pulp exposure, containing decayed material, negative probing and percussion tests. Tooth 22 shows a fistula on the buccal mucosa at the apical area, with extensive dark carious lesions on the distal surface and pulp exposure, negative probing and percussion tests.
radiographs_examination: Teeth 12 and 22 show low-density images in the apical area.
diagnosis:
* Tooth 13: Chronic pulpitis
* Teeth 12 and 22: Apical periodontitis
treatment_plan: Root canal therapy and crown restoration for teeth 12, 13, and 22.
management: For teeth 12, 13, and 22, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to the treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered, followed by pulp chamber opening and pulp extirpation. The coronal third of the root canals was prepared with GG drills, and canal lengths were measured using an apex locator: 13 at 25mm, 12 at 17mm, and 22 at 22.5mm. examination: Tooth 22 is missing with a mesiodistal space of 9mm and an occlusogingival distance of 5mm. The alveolar ridge is depressed without supraeruption of the opposing tooth. Overall oral hygiene is fair with calculus and staining present. No significant occlusal or joint abnormalities. Tooth 21 shows grade II mobility, percussion sensitivity, and a visible crack on the labial surface with mild gingival inflammation.
radiographs_examination: Tooth 22: alveolar bone width of 8mm and height of 14mm. Tooth 21: low-density image at the apex.
diagnosis: Tooth 22: Dental arch defect. Tooth 21: Pulpitis.
management: For tooth 22, informed consent was obtained for oral implant restoration. Under local anesthesia, a horizontal incision was made at the alveolar crest, the flap was elevated, and the site was prepared for implant placement. A Nobel implant (3.5*1.5mm) was inserted with a cover screw, and bone grafting was performed on the buccal side. The flap was sutured with tension relief, and a radiograph confirmed the implant position. The procedure lasted from 15:50 to 16:10. An impression was taken for the design of a temporary prosthesis. For tooth 21, local anesthesia was administered, the pulp chamber was accessed, canals were cleaned, length measured at 19mm, irrigated, and temporarily sealed with calcium hydroxide.
medical_instructions: Suture removal is scheduled for 1-2 weeks.

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: dental arch defect (K08.100×002). Treatment: implant restoration.
chief_complaint: The patient reports missing lower right posterior tooth for several months and requests restoration.
present_illness: The patient has experienced missing lower right posterior tooth for several months, affecting mastication.
past_medical_record: The patient is generally healthy with no significant medical history. Denies systemic diseases.
examination: Tooth 45 is missing with a mesiodistal gap of 7mm and an occlusogingival distance of 5mm. The alveolar ridge is depressed, and there is no overeruption of the opposing tooth. Overall oral hygiene is fair with calculus and staining present. No significant abnormalities in occlusion or temporomandibular joint.
radiographs_examination: Tooth 45 shows an alveolar bone width of 7mm and height of 10mm.
treatment_plan: Implant restoration for tooth 45.
management: Informed consent was obtained from the patient after explaining the procedure. Preoperative antibiotics were administered. Standard disinfection and draping were performed. Local infiltration anesthesia with articaine was used. A horizontal incision was made at the crest of the alveolar ridge, followed by full-thickness flap reflection. The site was prepared, and a BEGO implant (4.1x8.5 mm) was placed with a cover screw. Bone graft material was applied, and the flap was sutured with tension-free closure. A postoperative radiograph confirmed the implant position.
medical_instructions: Strictly follow post-implant surgery care instructions. Take prescribed oral antibiotics. Return for follow-up if any discomfort arises. Suture removal in two weeks.

management_cn: 45号牙齿，医生已履行告知义务，患者完全知情同意并签署《口腔种植修复知情同意书》。术前常规服用抗生素，常规消毒铺巾，复方阿替卡因适量局部浸润麻醉，在牙槽嵴顶做水平切口，全层切开粘骨膜，翻瓣，定位，备洞至预定深度，植入bego种植体，型号：4.1*8.5 mm，旋入覆盖螺丝，植入骨粉，覆盖骨膜。减张缝合，拍片位置可。
medical_instructions_cn: 严格遵守《种植术后注意事项》,口服抗生素，不适随诊。两周后拆线。

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: residual root (K08.300x002), chronic periapical periodontitis (K04.500). Treatment: post-extraction implant restoration, root canal therapy.
chief_complaint: The patient reports a residual root in the lower left posterior region for several months.
present_illness: The patient has had a residual root in the lower left posterior region for several months and seeks restoration.
past_medical_record: The patient is generally healthy with no significant medical history. Denies systemic diseases.
examination: Tooth 34 shows a residual root with caries and grade II mobility, negative to probing and percussion. Tooth 35 has a wedge-shaped defect on the buccal cervical area with black discoloration extending to deep dentin. There is a buccal sinus tract, negative to palpation, probing, cold, heat, and percussion tests, with grade II mobility.
radiographs_examination: Tooth 35 shows a large periapical radiolucency.
diagnosis: Tooth 34, residual root (K08.300x002). Tooth 35, chronic periapical periodontitis (K04.500).
treatment_plan: Tooth 34, post-extraction implant restoration. Tooth 35, root canal therapy.
management: For tooth 35, rubber dam isolation was achieved, occlusion adjusted, caries removed, pulp chamber accessed, and pulp chamber roof removed. One canal was located, pulp extirpated, and canal prepared using GG drills and rotary files up to F2. Canal length was determined to be 18.5mm using an apex locator. The canal was irrigated with sodium hypochlorite and saline, dried, and left open. The buccal wedge defect was restored with resin.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. Return for follow-up in two weeks.

radiographs_examination_cn: 35号牙齿，根尖周低密度影范围较大。
treatment_plan_cn: 34号牙齿，拔除后种植修复。35号牙齿，根管治疗。
management_cn: 35号牙齿，上橡皮障，调颌，去腐开髓，揭髓顶，探查根管口有一个，拔髓；GG钻预备根上三分之一，10#K锉探查根管长度，根测仪测量长度为18.5mm。大锥度根向预备技术预备根管，机扩至F2;次氯酸钠和生理盐水交替冲洗，吸干，开放。颊侧楔缺部树脂充填。

diagnosis: Teeth 25, 26: Tooth structure defect (K07.303). Tooth 26: Chronic apical periodontitis (K04.500).
management: Tooth 26: The patient was informed of the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Access opening was performed, canal orifices were explored, MB2 was located, and the coronal third was prepared with GG drills. Canal length was determined to be 18mm using an apex locator. The canal was prepared using a large taper rotary technique up to F2. The canal was irrigated with 1% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water using ultrasonic activation, alternating with sodium hypochlorite and saline, and dried with paper points. Calcium hydroxide paste was placed as a temporary dressing.
medical_instructions: Follow up if discomfort occurs. Maintain oral hygiene.

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: Dental arch defect (K08.100x002). (Poor restoration). Chronic apical periodontitis (K04.500). Treatment: Option 1: Root canal treatment for teeth 15 and 34, crown removal and implant restoration for teeth 14, 35, and 36. Option 2: Root canal treatment for tooth 15, crown removal and implant restoration for tooth 14, crown removal for teeth 34, 35, and 36, extraction of tooth 34, and implant-supported bridge restoration. The patient chose option 1.
chief_complaint: The patient reports pain in both sides of the mouth for several days.
present_illness: The patient describes continuous pain in both sides of the mouth for several days, with gingival swelling, seeking treatment.
past_medical_record: No significant medical history.
examination: Teeth 14, 35, and 36 are missing, with self-curing resin material and wire fixation to adjacent teeth, soft tissue swelling. Tooth 15 shows distal surface discoloration, a buccal sinus tract, soft tissue proliferation, mobility grade II, and percussion pain (++). Tooth 34 has buccal soft tissue swelling, a wedge-shaped groove at the cervical area with smooth edges, black surface, soft probing, pulp exposure, mobility grade II, negative cold test, and percussion pain (++).
radiographs_examination: Teeth 15 and 34 show low-density images in the apical region, with buccal alveolar bone resorption to the apex for tooth 34.
diagnosis: Teeth 14, 35, and 36: Dental arch defect (K08.100x002). (Poor restoration). Teeth 15 and 34: Chronic apical periodontitis (K04.500).
treatment_plan: Option 1: Root canal treatment for teeth 15 and 34, crown removal and implant restoration for teeth 14, 35, and 36. Option 2: Root canal treatment for tooth 15, crown removal and implant restoration for tooth 14, crown removal for teeth 34, 35, and 36, extraction of tooth 34, and implant-supported bridge restoration. The patient chose option 1.
management: For teeth 14, 35, and 36, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine was administered, and crowns were removed. For teeth 15 and 34, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Pulp chamber access was performed, pulp roof was removed, canal orifices were explored, and pulp was extirpated. GG drills were used to prepare the coronal third of the canal, and an 08# C-file was used to explore canal length. An apex locator measured the palatal root length at 18mm, buccal root length at 18mm, and tooth 34 length at 18mm. Canals were prepared using large taper rotary technique, and nickel-titanium files were used to enlarge to F2. Canals were ultrasonically irrigated with 1% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water, alternately rinsed with sodium hypochlorite and saline, dried, and temporarily sealed with calcium hydroxide paste.
medical_instructions: Return if discomfort occurs. Avoid biting hard objects. Follow-up in one week.

examination: Teeth 15 and 34 are temporarily sealed, with normal mucosa in the apical area, no percussion pain. Tooth 15 shows no mobility, tooth 34 shows grade I mobility.
management: For tooth 15, the patient was informed about the pros and cons of various restorative materials, associated costs, treatment time, possible follow-up visits, and complications, and voluntarily chose cast post and all-ceramic crown restoration. Temporary seal was removed, occlusion was adjusted, and cracks on the occlusal and mesial pulp wall were examined, extending beyond the mesial margin to subgingival. Post space was prepared, silicone rubber impression was taken, silicone rubber bite record was made, and temporary crown restoration was performed. Shade matching was done. For tooth 34, the patient was informed about the pros and cons of various restorative materials, associated costs, treatment time, possible follow-up visits, and complications, and voluntarily chose fiber post and all-ceramic crown restoration. Temporary seal was removed, post space was prepared, fiber post was placed, resin filling was done, and occlusion was adjusted and polished.
medical_instructions: Return if discomfort occurs. Avoid biting excessively hard foods, maintain oral hygiene, and attend follow-up appointments as scheduled. Advised that if the tooth cracks or there is recurrent pain after long-term restoration, extraction may be recommended.

past_medical_record: No significant medical history. Denies systemic diseases, hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, and drug allergies.
examination: Tooth 41 shows severe gingival recession, mobility grade III, negative probing, and percussion. Other teeth show moderate to severe gingival recession, bleeding on probing, periodontal pockets, and mobility grades I-II. Poor oral hygiene with gingival redness and loss of stippling. Tooth 11 shows discoloration with a metal post visible on the lingual side, negative percussion.

Local disinfection with povidone-iodine and local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine were administered. After anesthesia, the gingiva was separated and the tooth extracted with forceps. Routine curettage of the extraction socket and pressure hemostasis were performed. The extracted tooth was reshaped and bonded to adjacent teeth. For teeth 31, 32, 33, 34, 42, 43, 44, the patient was informed and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine was used, followed by subgingival scaling and root planing, with irrigation using hydrogen peroxide and saline. Oral hygiene instruction was provided, including brushing, flossing, and interdental brush use. For tooth 11, the patient was informed about the pros and cons of various restorative materials, costs, time, potential follow-up visits, and complications, and chose all-ceramic crown restoration. Tooth preparation, fine-tuning, silicone impression, bite registration, and temporary crown placement were performed. Shade matching was done.
medical_instructions: Strictly follow post-extraction care instructions. Take oral antibiotics as needed. Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs.

examination: Tooth 11 exhibits multiple soft tissue contusions on the lower lip. The labial incisal edge is fractured at the middle third, and the palatal side is fractured from the middle third to the cervical third junction. There is an enamel defect extending subgingivally on the palatal mesial third, with visible hairline cracks and a pulp exposure point approximately 1mm in diameter at the mesial pulp horn. The tooth is not mobile, and surrounding soft tissues appear normal.
radiographs_examination: No significant widening of the periodontal ligament space is observed for tooth 11.
diagnosis: Tooth 11: Tooth structure loss (K07.303) due to dental trauma and soft tissue contusion of the lower lip.
treatment_plan: Root canal therapy for tooth 11.
treatment_recommendations: Observe tooth 11 for one month post-root canal therapy. If asymptomatic, proceed with post and crown restoration. Consider extraction if prognosis is poor.
management: The patient was informed about the diagnosis, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to the treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine was administered, followed by pulp chamber opening and pulp removal. The coronal third of the canal was prepared with GG drills, and the canal length was determined to be 18mm using an apex locator. The canal was prepared using a large taper rotary technique with NiTi files up to F3. The canal was ultrasonically irrigated with 1% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water, and a master cone was fitted. The canal was dried with paper points and obturated with sealer and gutta-percha. A post-operative radiograph confirmed adequate filling. Composite resin was used for coronal restoration, followed by shaping, occlusal adjustment, and polishing.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs. Avoid biting hard objects. Schedule a follow-up appointment in one month.

management: For tooth 22, under rubber dam isolation, the cotton pellet was removed, and the root canal was ultrasonically irrigated with 2.5% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water. A temporary seal with paste and glass ionomer was placed. A post-operative radiograph confirmed proper filling. For tooth 24, the temporary crown and sealant were removed, the abutment and restoration were cleaned, and the restoration was tried in for marginal fit and proximal contact. After patient approval, it was cemented with dual-cure resin cement, occlusion adjusted, and polished.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: dental crowding; periapical periodontitis; occlusal caries; deep distal caries. Treatment: sequential extractions; staged fillings; base filling.
chief_complaint: Referred from orthodontics for tooth extraction to reduce crowding.
past_medical_record: The patient is generally healthy with no systemic diseases or drug allergies.
examination: Teeth 14 and 24 show crowding with no abnormalities or discomfort. Tooth 36 has a residual root with grade III mobility. Teeth 25, 26, 27, 38, 47, and 48 have occlusal caries, dark in color, with no cold sensitivity, percussion pain, gingival inflammation, or mobility. Tooth 37 has distal occlusal and buccal carious defects.
radiographs_examination: CBCT shows a low-density area at the apex of tooth 36. Tooth 37 has caries extending into the dentin.
diagnosis: Teeth 14 and 24: dental crowding. Tooth 36: periapical periodontitis. Teeth 25, 26, 27, 37, 38, 47, 48: occlusal caries. Tooth 37: deep distal caries.
treatment_plan: Sequential extraction of teeth 14, 24, and 36. Staged fillings for teeth 25, 26, 27, 38, 47, and 48. Base filling for tooth 37.
management: For teeth 25, 26, and 27, the patient was informed of the diagnosis, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis and consented to treatment. Caries removal, cavity preparation, etching, isolation, bonding, and layered VOCO resin filling were performed, followed by occlusal adjustment and polishing. Teeth 24 and 36 were extracted using local infiltration anesthesia, gingival separation, atraumatic extraction, curettage, repositioning, and hemostasis. Teeth 37, 38, 47, and 48 are scheduled for future fillings. Tooth 14 is scheduled for extraction.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms occur, return for root canal therapy. Follow post-extraction care instructions and take prescribed antibiotics as needed. Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation.
examination: Tooth 36 shows dark occlusal pits with slight resistance on probing, no percussion sensitivity. Teeth 42 and 43 exhibit gingival papillae redness and swelling, periodontal pockets, subgingival calculus, and bleeding on probing.
management: For tooth 36, caries removal and cavity preparation were performed. A matrix band and wedge were placed. The cavity was cleaned and dried, and a calcium hydroxide liner was applied near the pulp. Acid etching was followed by rinsing and drying. A bonding agent was applied, thinned, and light-cured. German VOCO resin was layered, light-cured, shaped, occlusion adjusted, and polished. For teeth 42 and 43, subgingival scaling and root planing were done under local anesthesia, followed by irrigation with hydrogen peroxide and saline, and application of Periochip. Oral hygiene instruction was provided, including brushing, flossing, and interdental brush use.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Maintain oral hygiene with regular mouthwash use. Schedule regular check-ups and seek immediate care if discomfort arises.

Overall oral hygiene is fair, with calculus and staining present.
treatment_plan: In-office bleaching for teeth 11, 12, 13, 14, 21, 22, 23, 24, 31, 32, 33, 34, 41, 42, 43, 44. Patient consent obtained.
management: Teeth 11, 12, 13, 14, 21, 22, 23, 24, 31, 32, 33, 34, 41, 42, 43, 44 were photographed and shade recorded as C2. Teeth were polished and rinsed.
