past_medical_record: No history of hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, hepatitis, or tuberculosis. No known allergies. No recent travel to high-risk areas or contact with COVID-19 cases.
examination: Oral hygiene is average with slight pigmentation on tooth surfaces. Significant calculus, especially on the lingual side of the lower anterior teeth and buccal side of posterior teeth. Gingival margins are red, soft, and thickened with blunt papillae. Gingival sulcus depth is 1 mm, BI:1, DI:1, with no attachment loss.
treatment_plan: Supragingival scaling with ultrasonic and air polishing.
management: Oral hygiene education was provided, including brushing technique and floss use. The patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis and consented to treatment. Plaque disclosing agent was applied, followed by rinsing, air polishing, and full-mouth supragingival scaling. Enamel was sealed for caries prevention, and steam eye masks and iodine glycerin were applied.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Avoid pigmented beverages like coffee, tea, and cola, and refrain from smoking. Maintain oral hygiene with mouthwash. Schedule regular check-ups and return if discomfort occurs.

management: For teeth 31 and 41, temporary crowns were removed, abutments and restorations were cleaned, and the fit of the restoration was checked. medical_instructions: 1. Initial denture wear may cause foreign body sensation, nausea, increased salivation, and speech difficulties, which will improve with practice. 2. Avoid biting hard foods for the first 1-2 weeks; start with small, soft foods and gradually increase hardness and size as you adapt. 3. Use the correct method for inserting and removing dentures, aligning them properly and gently pushing them into place. Avoid excessive force or biting to prevent damage or deformation. 4. Clean dentures thoroughly, removing food debris after meals. Soak dentures in water overnight after cleaning. Use denture cleaning tablets regularly. 5. Maintain cleanliness of remaining teeth with proper brushing and regular scaling. Avoid hard and sticky foods. If looseness or discomfort occurs, schedule a follow-up appointment, and call ahead to book.

management: For teeth 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 31, 32, 33, and 34, subgingival curettage and root planing were performed under local anesthesia, followed by irrigation with hydrogen peroxide and saline, and application of PerioChip. Oral hygiene instruction (OHI) was provided, including brushing, flossing, and interdental brush use. patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Chronic periodontitis; combined periodontal-endodontic lesion. Treatment: Systematic periodontal therapy and root canal treatment.
chief_complaint: The patient reports tooth mobility and pain when biting with the front teeth for several months.
present_illness: Gradual onset of tooth mobility and weakness in chewing for several months, with pain in the front teeth when biting for several weeks.
past_medical_record: Denies systemic diseases, hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, and drug allergies. No significant family history. No symptoms of fever, cough, fatigue, or loss of taste or smell. The patient has a history of smoking.
examination: Moderate to severe gingival recession throughout the mouth, with bleeding on probing. Deep periodontal pockets of 15 mm on the mesial and distal surfaces of tooth 11, positive cold and percussion tests, and Grade I mobility. Spacing between teeth 11 and 21. Poor oral hygiene; DI:2, CI:2 with supragingival calculus covering less than 2/3 of the tooth surface, detectable attachment loss, and subgingival calculus with bleeding index: 4.
diagnosis: Chronic periodontitis. Combined periodontal-endodontic lesion on tooth 11.
treatment_plan: Systematic periodontal therapy. Root canal treatment for tooth 11.
management: Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine in the upper right region, subgingival scaling, root planing, laser treatment, and irrigation with hydrogen peroxide and saline. Oral hygiene instruction provided, including brushing, flossing, and interdental brush use. For tooth 11, access opening, pulp extirpation, preparation of the coronal third with GG drills, root canal length determination with an apex locator (21 mm), preparation with large taper technique to F2, alternating irrigation with sodium hypochlorite and saline, drying, and temporary sealing with calcium hydroxide paste. Diagnostic wax-up for the anterior region.
medical_instructions: Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Maintain oral hygiene and use mouthwash. Schedule regular follow-ups and return if discomfort occurs.

past_medical_record: No history of hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, hepatitis, tuberculosis, or contact with infectious diseases. No allergies reported. No recent travel to high-risk areas or contact with COVID-19 cases.
examination: Overall oral hygiene is moderate, with some pigmentation on the teeth. treatment_plan: Supragingival scaling with ultrasonic and air polishing.
management: Oral hygiene instructions were provided, including brushing techniques and flossing. management: Tooth 46: The temporary resin was removed, and the inlay was tried in for marginal fit and contact. The tooth was etched, rinsed, dried, and isolated. Bonding agent was applied to both the tooth and inlay, and dual-cure resin cement was applied to the inlay's internal surface. management: Tooth 31: Removable partial denture was placed successfully with good retention and stability. Occlusion was adjusted and polished.
medical_instructions: 1. Initial denture wear may cause foreign body sensation, including nausea, increased salivation, and speech difficulties, which will improve with practice. 2. Avoid hard foods during the first 1-2 weeks of wearing the denture; start with small, soft foods and gradually increase hardness and size as you adapt. 3. Learn the correct method of inserting and removing the denture, aligning it with the teeth and gently pushing it into place. Avoid excessive force or biting the denture into place, which could damage or deform it. 4. Maintain denture hygiene by cleaning food debris after meals and soaking the denture in water overnight. Regularly use denture cleaning tablets. 5. Maintain oral hygiene of remaining teeth with proper brushing and regular dental cleanings.

chief_complaint: Referred from orthodontics for tooth extraction.
present_illness: Referred from orthodontics seeking tooth extraction.
examination: Tooth 14 is intact with healthy gingiva. Tooth 48 is unerupted with healthy gingiva. Teeth 17, 27, 37, and 47 have occlusal caries, negative percussion, healthy gingiva, and normal cold test response.
diagnosis:
* Tooth 14: Dental crowding (K07.302) with reduction in tooth number.
* Tooth 48: Potential impaction (K01.100).
* Teeth 17, 27, 37, 47: Dental caries (K02.901).
treatment_plan:
* Extraction of teeth 14 and 48.
* Resin restoration for teeth 17, 27, 37, and 47.
management: For tooth 48, local disinfection with povidone-iodine was performed, followed by inferior alveolar nerve block anesthesia with lidocaine and local infiltration with articaine. After anesthesia onset, gingival separation and crown sectioning were done, and the tooth was extracted with forceps. The extraction site was curetted and sutured for hemostasis. For tooth 14, local disinfection and infiltration anesthesia were applied, followed by gingival separation and extraction with forceps. The site was curetted and compressed for hemostasis. For teeth 17, 27, 37, and 47, caries removal gel was applied, caries were excavated, cavities were prepared, cleaned, and dried. Acid etching, bonding agent application, and layered resin filling were performed, followed by occlusal adjustment and polishing.
medical_instructions: Follow up if discomfort occurs. Bite on gauze for 40 minutes. Avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours. Eat after 2 hours, avoiding hot foods.

examination: Tooth 22 is temporarily sealed. Teeth 17, 46, and 47 have occlusal caries extending to the middle dentin layer, with normal cold and heat tests. Teeth 14, 24, 34, and 44 are fully erupted and require extraction as per orthodontic consultation.
diagnosis: Moderate caries of teeth 17, 46, and 47 (K02.800x007); malocclusion of teeth 14, 24, 34, and 44.
treatment_plan: Fillings for teeth 17, 46, and 47; extractions for teeth 14, 24, 34, and 44.
management: For tooth 22, isolation was applied, temporary seal was removed, medicament was retrieved, and the pulp chamber was accessed. One canal was located, and pulp extirpation was incomplete with slight bleeding. Hand files were used to negotiate the canal to size 15, with a working length of 22.5mm. Canal preparation was done using NiTi rotary instruments with Glyde assistance. The canal was irrigated, dried, and the master cone was trial-fitted to working length. The canal was obturated with warm gutta-percha, a base was placed, and the access was filled with composite. For teeth 17, 46, and 47, carious dentin was removed to the deep dentin layer without pulp exposure. Shade matching was done, gingival retraction was applied, and the proximal restoration system was used. Pulp protection and base placement were followed by composite restoration, occlusal adjustment, and polishing. For teeth 14 and 44, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and risks, and consented to extractions. Local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine was administered, gingiva was separated, teeth were luxated and extracted, sockets were curetted, irrigated with saline, and gelatin sponges were placed for hemostasis.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs. Bite on cotton roll for 40 minutes, avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours, and avoid eating for 2 hours. Recommend avoiding very hot foods.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Periodontitis.
chief_complaint: The patient returns for a follow-up one week after periodontal treatment.
present_illness: The patient reports no significant discomfort and returns for continued periodontal treatment.
examination: The gingiva in the left region shows good healing, with no significant abnormalities elsewhere.
management: In the upper right region, 4% articaine was used for local infiltration anesthesia, followed by subgingival scaling, root planing, and laser treatment. The area was irrigated with hydrogen peroxide and saline. Oral hygiene instruction (OHI) was provided, including brushing, flossing, and interdental brush use. Teeth 17 and 18 were disinfected with povidone-iodine, anesthetized with 4% articaine, and the gingiva was separated. The teeth were luxated and extracted with forceps. The extraction sites were curetted, gelatin silver was placed in the sockets, and pressure and sutures were applied for hemostasis.
medical_instructions: Strictly follow post-extraction care instructions. Avoid acidic foods and extreme temperatures for one week. Maintain oral hygiene with mouthwash. Schedule regular check-ups and return if discomfort occurs.

chief_complaint: Mobility in the upper left posterior tooth.
examination: Tooth 16 has occlusal caries reaching mid-dentin, negative to probing, cold, heat, and percussion tests. Retained tooth [ED][0] shows grade II mobility. Teeth 44 and 45 are erupting buccally. No other abnormalities noted.
diagnosis: Moderate caries in tooth 16; retained tooth [ED][0].
treatment_plan: Filling for tooth 16; extraction of retained tooth [ED][0].
management: For tooth 16, a rubber dam was placed, caries removed, and cavity prepared. Calcium hydroxide was applied near the pulp. The tooth was extracted with forceps, and hemostasis was achieved by compression.
medical_instructions: Strictly follow post-extraction care instructions. Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs.

radiographs_examination: Tooth 37 site shows adequate bone volume and quality.

management: For tooth 37, the patient was fully informed and consented to the procedure. Preoperative antibiotics were administered. patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Dental arch defect.
chief_complaint: Missing upper right posterior tooth for several months, seeking restoration.
present_illness: The upper right posterior tooth has been missing for several months, affecting eating. The patient seeks restoration.
past_medical_record: Healthy with no significant medical history.
examination: Teeth 16 and 41 are missing, with a mesiodistal gap of 9mm and an occlusogingival distance of 5mm. The alveolar ridge is resorbed with no overeruption of opposing teeth. Oral hygiene is fair with calculus (+) and pigmentation (+). No significant occlusal or joint abnormalities.
radiographs_examination: Teeth 16 and 41 show alveolar bone width of 8mm and height of 10mm.
diagnosis: Dental arch defect at teeth 16 and 41.
management: For tooth 16, the patient was fully informed and consented to the oral implant restoration procedure. Standard disinfection and draping were performed. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered. A horizontal incision was made at the alveolar ridge crest, and a full-thickness flap was elevated. The site was prepared to the planned depth, and a Bego implant (size 4.1x10 mm) was placed with a cover screw. Tension-free suturing was performed, and radiographic verification of placement was done. For tooth 41, an impression was taken for a Maryland bridge design.
medical_instructions: Sutures to be removed in 1-2 weeks.

examination: Teeth 14 and 15 exhibit cervical wedge defects with pulp exposure. The mucosa in the apical region is normal, and both teeth show positive percussion.

management: For teeth 14 and 15, rubber dam isolation was applied, and temporary seals were removed. The pulp chamber was accessed, and the canal orifices were explored. Pulp extirpation was performed. GG drills were used to prepare the coronal third of the canal, and an 08# C file was used to determine the canal length, measured at 19mm with an apex locator. Canals were prepared using a large taper technique and machine files to F2. Ultrasonic irrigation with 1% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water was performed, alternating with saline, and the canals were dried. Calcium hydroxide paste was placed as a temporary seal.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Pulpitis. Treatment: Root canal therapy.
chief_complaint: Follow-up visit.
examination: Tooth 24 shows ink-like discoloration on the distal proximal surface, with probe retention reaching deep dentin, and sensitivity to cold stimuli.
treatment_plan: Root canal therapy for tooth 24.
management: Tooth 24: The patient was informed about the condition and consented to treatment. Under rubber dam isolation, caries removal was performed using high-speed handpiece and slow-speed round bur, followed by pulp chamber opening, pulp extirpation, and canal negotiation. The canals were irrigated with saline, and canal length was determined (17, 19 mm) using an electronic apex locator. Nickel-titanium rotary files were used to prepare the canals to size F2. The canals were disinfected with 2.5% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water, and a trial fit of the master cone was taken. After irrigation, drying, and isolation, the canals were dried with paper points and obturated using SP and gutta-percha with vertical compaction. A post-operative radiograph confirmed proper filling. Post space preparation was done, and a fiber post was bonded. The tooth was prepared and refined for a crown. A silicone impression and bite registration were taken, and a temporary crown was placed.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if any discomfort occurs.

management: For tooth 36, the tooth surface was polished, and the inlay was tried in. The inlay and tooth surface were treated with hydrofluoric acid etching for 90 seconds, rinsed, and dried. Occlusion was adjusted, polished, and photographed.
